core_obligations: Make the covering finite (proof lines 11768-11772): the constructible topology on a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme has a quasi-compact underlying space, so finitely many of the given pieces suffice.

Split each piece into locally constant parts (proof lines 11772-11781): each piece is itself quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the characterization by finite partitions applies and produces locally closed constructible parts on which the sheaf is finite locally constant.

Refine to a partition of the whole scheme (proof lines 11781-11785): constructibility of a constructible subset in a constructible subset is used to see that the pieces remain constructible in the ambient scheme, and the refinement lemma produces the desired finite partition, to which the characterization is applied once more.
proof_roadmap: Reduce the covering to a finite one using quasi-compactness in the constructible topology.
Apply the partition characterization on each piece to get finite local constancy there.
Assemble a partition of the whole scheme using the constructibility and refinement results.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a sheaf which is constructible after restriction to the members of a covering by constructible locally closed subschemes is itself constructible (statement lines 11758-11766). The proof is a complete reduction: the covering is made finite through the quasi-compactness of the constructible topology (proof lines 11768-11772); each piece is shown to be quasi-compact and quasi-separated so that the partition characterization of constructibility applies, producing parts on which the sheaf is finite locally constant (proof lines 11772-11781); and the parts are reassembled into a finite constructible partition of the whole scheme using the two topological inputs, after which the characterization gives constructibility (proof lines 11781-11785). The non-formal content is the sequence of reductions and the transport of constructibility. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with every input named.
